data.title: History & Batch Tracking
data.goalStatement: The History tab plus the local persistence layer behind it: every batch ever sent is recorded with its frozen frame, per-annotation records, generated prompt and hierarchy dump, and listed grouped by time period with a thumbnail crop, title/summary, timestamp and status chip (Fixed, In progress, etc.). All records survive app restarts and never leave the machine. Why: PER-2 needs to see what has already been reported and its state without re-testing everything, and the Verify loop needs a durable original-frame record to diff against.

sources.summary: Upstream PRD feature bundle F-8 'History & Batch Tracking' (sourcePrd: rectify). Carries FR-20, NFR-4, NFR-7, AC-22, AC-33, SC-8, SC-15, US-8, dependsOn: [F-7], priority: must, phase: PH-1, estimate: M.

Bundled prototype containing the History tab UI. Decoded modules in raw/design/ (History markup: raw/design/_history-tab.html, full screen: raw/design/6833ecee.html). Tab-strip position (third segment), in-progress badge, grouped-by-time list, row anatomy with 44×44 crop thumbnail and exact measurements, status chips with tone dots, optional Verify button (scope boundary to F-9), footer session line.

codeReferences.note: F-7's cross-process handoff contract: AnnotationEnvelope, AnnotationHandoff interface, FileSlotAnnotationHandoff at ~/.rectify/handoff/latest.json. F-8 must persist every batch sent, not just latest.
F-7's MCP server reads the handoff slot. F-8 must coordinate with this reader's lifecycle (never delete active published batches).
Room KMP scaffold (currently unused, first intended consumer is F-8). Must wire Room's KSP for desktop target. registry/features.json names it 'scaffold only'.
The right inspector panel with tab strip; F-8 adds the History segment (third tab). Existing Annotations and Payload tabs already there.

designReferences.description: Complete History tab design. Tab-strip placement (third segment), in-progress badge count, vertically scrolling grouped list (Today/Yesterday headers), rows with flex-gap-10px layout, 44×44 thumbnail crop with box-shadow 1px var(--line2), title 12.5px single-line-ellipsis, meta-line Mono 10.5px var(--ink3) '3 notes · 14:02 · #a41f', status row with 20px chip (11px/500 font, border-radius 10px, tone dot), optional sub-line Mono 10px (agent activity), optional Verify button 22px (11.5px/500, background var(--primary)), footer with agent/path/session line.

Extracted History markup block from prototype. Crop math from design: cx=max(0,x-pad); cy=max(0,y-pad); cw=min(W-cx,w+2pad); ch=min(H-cy,h+2pad); s=min(bw/cw, bh/ch); box = cw*s × ch*s, frame offset -cx*s,-cy*s, scale(s). Statuses: Sent/In progress (amber)/Fixed (green)/Verified (neutral)/Follow-up sent (red). Frame 296×640 scaled to fit 44×44 box.

existingSolutions.summary: F-7 (resolve-and-send-mcp, merged) publishes each send to ~/.rectify/handoff/latest.json with AnnotationEnvelope containing frame bytes, crop bytes, hierarchy dump, prompt, version, sentAtMs. F-8 must read this contract and persist every send in a database, keyed by sentAtMs or similar.
F-4 (drag-annotate-frozen-frame) defines StagedAnnotation, FrozenFrame, DeviceRect models. F-8 must store these per-batch in the database and reconstruct them for the History UI.

glossary.definition: A single Resolve & Send operation: one frozen frame, N annotations on it, one hierarchy dump, one generated prompt, one sentAtMs timestamp. Published atomically by F-7 to ~/rectify/handoff/latest.json, must be persisted by F-8.

A colored chip (Sent/In progress/Fixed/Verified/Follow-up sent) shown per row in History, preceded by a tone dot. Status transitions are mostly F-9's territory (Verify), but Sent is the entry state, In progress indicates MCP agent is working, Follow-up sent is a secondary send after fixes.
The original adb-captured PNG screenshot at the moment Resolve & Send was clicked. Stored by F-7 at ~/.rectify/handoff/<sentAtMs>/frame.png. F-8 must persist a reference to this or a copy of it.
A 44×44 preview extracted from the frozen frame, centered on the annotated element (or elements if multi-annotation batch). Crop math defined in design: pad=18, bw/bh=40/40, scale to fit.
Grouping header in History list: 'Today', 'Yesterday', 'Last week', etc. Design prototype shows Today/Yesterday; full bucketing algorithm undefined.
Footer of History list showing 'claude · ~/code/shopkit · session 7f3a' — agent name, project path, session identifier. Source of this data (per-batch or global?) undefined.
Optional sub-line under status chip for in-progress batches, e.g. 'editing CartScreen.kt'. Indicates live MCP agent work. Source (MCP response? heartbeat?) undefined.

ambiguities: Status transition rules and state machine: what moves a batch from Sent → In progress → Fixed → Verified? Verify is F-9, but what triggers Sent → In progress? Does the MCP agent publish status updates, or does the Verify flow (F-9) perform all transitions?
Follow-up sent status: mentioned in design but not defined in any requirement. Is this a state users can manually trigger, or automatic after a Verify → Fix cycle?

Session line footer data source: design shows 'claude · ~/code/shopkit · session 7f3a' but where does this live per-batch? Is it in AnnotationEnvelope? Is it the session from the MCP get_latest_annotation call?

Activity line (sub-line under status chip): 'editing CartScreen.kt' is shown for in-progress batches in the design, but no requirement defines where this data comes from. Is it polled from the MCP agent? A heartbeat? Part of AnnotationEnvelope?
History list bucketing: design shows 'Today' and 'Yesterday' groups, but full algorithm for time-period bucketing is undefined. Is it just Today/Yesterday/Older? Weekly buckets? Arbitrary?
Search/filter affordances: no requirement mentions searching or filtering History. Is the tab a flat vertically-scrolling list only?
Pagination/max-visible: no requirement on History list size. Does it paginate, virtualize, or show all? Memory cost for hundreds/thousands of batches?
Navigation after row click: clicking a History row — does it open the Verify flow immediately (F-9 territory)? Or open a detail view?
Thumbnail crop on multi-annotation batches: if a batch has 3 annotations scattered across the frame, what single crop is shown in the thumbnail? First annotation? Bounding box? Centered on average?
Frame persistence: must F-8 store the full PNG frame bytes (per F-7's frame.png), or just a reference to the handoff directory, or generate thumbnails on-demand from memory?
Batch deletion: no requirement on whether users can delete batches. History grows unbounded? Or is there a retention policy?

Verify button visibility: AC-22 says rows show 'title/summary/timestamp/status chip' (no Verify button). SC-8 says 'Locate a Fixed batch, Click Verify'. Design shows Verify only on Fixed status rows. Is AC-22 incomplete, or is the Verify button out of scope for F-8?

Cross-platform: F-8 spec lists Android/iOS/Desktop targets, but F-7 (Resolve & Send) is desktop-only. Does F-8 also desktop-only, or does it span all platforms? Registry notes indicate History is desktop-specific (RectifyWindow is desktop only).
